newsitem.title: UK: UK physical grain markets hit by farmer resistance.
newsitem.headline: UK physical grain markets hit by farmer resistance.

text.p: The UK cash grain market quietened down on Thursday as farmers started to resist selling at current low prices, traders said.

"Whether its a question of avoiding the issue I don't know, but farm sellers seem increasingly willing to take a gamble on the possibility that things can't get much worse for them," one trade source said.
"Merchants seem convinced that farmers will have to sell at these prices because they're anticipating that sterling will remain strong," another said.
"But whatever sterling does now, I don't know how much this market can go down," he added.
Feelings were mixed as to whether the market had bottomed out but trade sources were unanimous in reporting limited activity after a flurry of selling by both merchants and farmers on Wednesday.
The FOB market was neglected on Thursday due to a combination of strong sterling and traders awaiting the results of the European Union tender, sources said.
In delivered market, prices were generally reported unchanged from the previous day's rates of 100 to 99.50 stg for April/June delivery in most areas.
Barley to Norfolk/Suffolk was traded at 100.00 stg, also for April/June but there were no reports of business in milling wheat 11 percent protein.
